1: The patient has bilateral breast lumps, with the left breast lump fixed to the chest wall and an irregular spiculated mass on MRI, which is suspicious for malignancy. Fine-needle aspiration cytology of the left breast lump revealed poorly cohesive clusters of ductal cells with pleomorphism, hyperchromasia, and prominent nucleoli, and the biopsy confirmed infiltrative duct cell carcinoma that was estrogen- and progesterone-receptor positive.
2: The right breast had a firm, mobile 1 × 1 cm lump in the lower outer quadrant, and MRI showed a well-defined lesion with a type 1 contrast enhancement pattern. FNAC of the right breast lump showed three-dimensional clusters of hyperchromatic cells with prominent nucleoli and scattered pleomorphic cells with mitotic figures admixed with benign ductal cells and myoepithelial cells, which is consistent with a fibroadenoma.

The patient has a firm, mobile lump in the right breast, a well-defined lesion on MRI with a type 1 contrast enhancement pattern, and three-dimensional clusters of hyperchromatic cells with prominent nucleoli on fine-needle aspiration cytology, all of which are consistent with fibroadenoma.
